topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text: I stepped into the artist’s studio, the air thick with the scent of oil paints and desperation. The walls were a testament to a tortured soul, canvases exploding with color and emotion. But there, in the corner, was the real exhibit—her work, reproduced permanently on some punk’s skin. The artist’s eyes were pools of stormy silence, the kind that tells you a whole lot without saying a word. I’ve seen that look before, the same one that glints in the eyes of the desperate and the wronged. She wanted justice, but more than that, she wanted her art back. Her way. Not defaced, not bastardized. I get that. I nodded, understanding more than she thought. “Let’s find who did this,” I said, the city’s rain already drumming a rhythm in my ears. This case, it’s different. It’s about more than the money. It’s about the line between creation and destruction.
